Ada legt dir eine Glasplatte hin, eine g: Ada puts a glass plate in front of you, exposed for an entire night. Bright trails cross Kettlegate from five directions. They all converge on one point: above the observatory.
Agnes Crane stellt die schwarzen Kerzen: Agnes Crane sets out the black candles, mourning her husband.
Akte: Der Brand von St. Ebba: File: the fire of St. Ebba
Am Gitter neben der Pfandhaustür hängt e: On the railing next to the pawnshop door hangs a lamplighter's coat with brass buttons. It is still dripping wet.
Black wax sticks to the edge of the step. A signet ring has pressed a sign into it: two crossed organ pipes. No eye in a circle. Beside it hangs a long grey hair.
Am Stiefelregal des Reviers: ein Paar Di: On the precinct's boot rack: a pair of service boots with yellow clay and grey ash on the soles. The same clay as in the churchyard of St. Ebba. No name inside.
An der Brücke wurde mit dem Augen-Siegel: At the bridge, something was sealed with the eye seal of the choir of St. Ebba.
Anselm finanziert mit Kerzenverkäufen de: Anselm funds the rebuilding of the chapel with candle sales.
Anselms Kassenbuch: Jede Münze stammt au: Anselm's cash book: every coin comes from candle sales and goes into rebuilding the chapel. Not a single grave good.
Auf dem Löschpapier, spiegelverkehrt: „…: On the blotting paper, mirror-reversed: “… was first at every crime scene … keeps the loot in his cabinet … ask him about the star …” The same sentences as in the letters to the precinct.
Auf dem Schreibtisch steht ein Glas Wass: On the desk stands a glass of water. Green threads float in it, duckweed. That's not tap water.
Auf dem Stein: „Lilian Vey, 7 Jahre“. Da: On the stone: “Lilian Vey, 7 years”. The grave has been freshly dug up, yellow clay piled beside it. In the coffin only the imprint of a small box. The spade marks have a distinctive notch.
Auf der letzten Seite stehen sieben Frau: On the last page are seven women's names, blackened with ash. Beside them a sentence in fresh ink: “Whoever has sung sings on. They wait in the bell.”
Barnaby hat Rook nachts gesehen. Rook ha: Barnaby saw Rook at night. Rook locked him away with a false report.
Barnaby hat die Silberleuchter von St. E: Barnaby stole the silver candlesticks of St. Ebba.
Benji ist der Junge, der durch Thornes K: Benji is the boy who came through Thorne's coal chute. In his sleep he brought the banker the canal water. The two cases are one.
Benji ist verschwunden. An seinem Bett k: Benji has disappeared. Coal dust sticks to his bed.
Benjis Bett ist gemacht, als hätte niema: Benji's bed is made as if nobody had slept in it. But on the sheet are black prints of small feet. Coal dust.
Bess Hagans Mann ist krank von verdorben: Bess Hagan's husband is ill from spoiled fish from their own barrel.
Bram denkt lange nach. „Knox. Hat’s verk: Bram thinks for a long time. “Knox. Sold it. To the professor. Twelve barrels.” Pause. “Delivery new moon. Observatory.” That's more words than he has ever said to you.
Bram sagt nicht viel. „Fässer weg. Nacht: Bram doesn't say much. “Barrels gone. At night. Finn has the key.” Then he falls silent again.
Constable Rook sang als Junge in Miriam: As a boy, Constable Rook sang in Miriam Vey's choir.
Constables tragen Hester aus der Krypta,:
Constables carry Hester out of the crypt, Moll is arrested. But when the constables return, the music box is gone.

Miriam Vey has what she wanted. She will try again.
Constables carry Hester out of the crypt. She wakes in the morning and remembers nothing but a song. Moll sits in the cell next to Barnaby.

Because you destroyed the music box, the ritual is broken. Somewhere in the city that night, a woman in a grey coat screams.

Marlowe puts a new file in front of you. On it: the eye in the circle.
Das Lied ist Miriam Veys Wiegenlied für: The song is Miriam Vey's lullaby for her daughter Lilian.
The song and the frost belong together. Something devoured the lantern's light. It was a ritual.
Das Lied, die Spieldose, das gestohlene: The song, the music box, the stolen light: Vey is trying to bring back her dead daughter. Hester was meant to pay for it.
Das Schlagwerk der Turmuhr wurde auf Vey: The striking mechanism of the tower clock was retuned to Vey's three notes.
Das Siegel des Chors an der Brücke und d: The choir's seal at the bridge and the woman who wanted Elias' key: Miriam Vey stood at the bridge last night.
Das Teleskop zeigt jetzt nach oben. Im O: The telescope now points upwards. In the eyepiece hangs the star, and small lights circle it. One hums like Madame Varenne, one is a shadow without a person, one laughs like a child in its sleep.
Das Wasser in Thornes Lunge stammt aus d: The water in Thorne's lungs comes from the Ashgrove canal.
Das Wundertonikum ist gefärbter Gin mit: The Miracle Tonic is coloured gin with laudanum. It makes you addicted, not ill.
Das fremde Silberbad stammt von den Spie: The strange silver bath comes from the mirrors of the cabinet at the North Gate.
Der Chor ist nicht zerschlagen: The choir is not broken up
Der Chor sammelt sich im Lagerhaus 7. Do: The choir gathers in Warehouse 7. That's where Rook disappears when he's not on watch.
Der Chor versammelt sich im Lagerhaus 7: The choir gathers in Warehouse 7 at the Canal Harbour.
Der Fremde auf den Platten ist Lucan Mew: The stranger on the plates is Lucan Mews. He takes the guests' shadows.
Der Frühzug fährt in ein paar Stunden. K:
The early train leaves in a few hours. Kettlegate still lies in the fog, the chimneys, the clock tower, the ruins of St. Ebba. A wanted poster with your face already hangs on every lantern.

In your coat pocket is a ticket to Wexmoor, issued in a name that isn't yours.

Chapter 2 begins: The Moor City.
Der Maler zeigt dir ein nasses Bild: sie: The painter shows you a wet painting: seven white figures in the fog, one behind the other, on their way to the canal. “I paint what I see. I just didn't understand that their mouths were open. They were singing, and then they were silent.”
Der Mann im Polizeimantel: The man in the police coat
Der Maskenmacher Jonas Pell hat Madame V: The mask maker Jonas Pell poisoned Madame Varenne.
Der Rattenfänger lockt die Kinder mit se: The rat catcher lures the children out of the house with his flute.
The rat catcher lures the children away with his flute.
Der Schlachtergehilfe Knox verkauft das: The butcher's assistant Knox secretly sells the ox blood to the Night Market.
Der Schlachterlehrling Finn ist der Mask: The butcher's apprentice Finn is the masked player who robs guests in the theatre.
Der Schminkspiegel der Diva ist von inne: The diva's make-up mirror is frosted from the inside. An eye in a circle has been drawn into the frost with a finger, from behind, as if someone had stood inside the mirror.
Der Souffleur Felix Dunmore sang früher: The prompter Felix Dunmore used to sing in Vey's choir.
Der Straßenjunge Kit hat Gretas Kasse ge: The street urchin Kit stole Greta's cash box.
Der Tote im Kontor: The dead man in the counting house
Der Webstuhl brennt schnell, wie trocken:
The loom burns quickly, like dry hair. Upstairs the children cry out in their sleep, then it is quiet, and for the first time they sleep without wandering.

Benji is only found in the morning, behind the loom, his feet black. He wakes up, but he no longer speaks. Molly sits with him every day.

Miss Wren is led away. Thorne's case is closed with it.
Der dreizehnte Gast ist ein Mensch, der: The thirteenth guest is a person made up of other people's shadows.
Der entlassene Schauspieler Lionel Crabb: The dismissed actor Lionel Crabb wears Pell's stolen mask and robs the guests.
Der erste Schlag soll in der Neumondnach: The first strike is to fall on the night of the new moon in the resonance chamber beneath the foundry.
Der stumme Maskenmacher war in der Garde: The mute mask maker was in the dressing room and mixed something into her powder.
Die Akte Elias Thorne wird geschlossen::
The Elias Thorne file is closed: accident under the influence of alcohol. You believed the police's own false story.

The next night the second lantern in Ashgrove Lane goes out.
Die Brückenlaterne ist erloschen. Das Gl: The bridge lantern has gone out. The glass is covered with frost from the inside, though the night is mild. The wick hasn't burned down.
Die Brückenlaterne wurde von etwas Kalte: The bridge lantern was put out by something cold.
Die Ginflasche an der Straße liegt seit: The gin bottle by the road has been lying there for days.
Die Glocke in der Brandnacht: The bell on the night of the fire
Die Glocke ist im Lagerhaus: The bell is in the warehouse
Die Kinder von St. Brigid wandeln nachts: The children of St. Brigid walk in their sleep at night.
Die Leuchter im Schaufenster: The candlesticks in the shop window
Die Linsenkästen sind leer, jeder Samtpl: The lens cases are empty, every velvet slot tidily cleared. The slippers stand neatly side by side at the door. People who are abducted don't pack first.
Die Neumondnacht: The night of the new moon
The vials shatter on the floorboards. A whirl of voices sweeps through the tower, laughing, weeping, singing all at once, then it is silent.

Some singers find their voice again, others only a croak. Madame Varenne has whispered ever since. Felix is led away.

That night the bell strikes once by itself, without anyone pulling the rope.
Die Platten wurden in einem fremden Silb: The plates were developed in a strange silver bath.
Die Rostbrüder gießen die Glocke für ihr: The Rust Brothers are casting the bell for their Rust Father.
Die Schlafwandler gehen zum Kanal und ta: The sleepwalkers go to the canal and dip their hands into the water.
Die Schlafwandler von St. Brigid tauchen: At night the sleepwalkers of St. Brigid dip their hands into the Ashgrove canal. The same water was in Thorne's lungs. The two cases are one.
The silver candlesticks were never stolen. Barnaby is in jail although innocent.
Die Spieldose spielt von selbst. Es ist: The music box plays by itself. It is the same melody as on the sheet music: the lullaby.
Die Spur führt zu M. Vey: The trail leads to M. Vey
Die Stimmen der sieben verschwundenen Sä: The voices of the seven missing singers were cast into the bell.
Die Stimmen wandern in den Uhrturm: The voices go to the clock tower
Die Stimmen werden genommen, nicht krank: The voices are taken, not sick. And the prompter was once Vey's choirboy. He collects voices for her.
Die Stimmgabel summt, um ein Haar danebe:
The tuning fork hums, a hair off. A crack runs through the bell, fine as a hair, then wider, and from it seven notes rise, one after another, and vanish up the stairs into the night.

In the morning seven women turn up at the city's hospitals, hoarse, confused, alive.

Miriam Vey sits on the floor of the chamber, her borrowed face in her hands. She doesn't resist when Price puts the handcuffs on her. She only hums. For the first time the song sounds right.
Die Turmuhr soll die gefangenen Stimmen: The tower clock is meant to make all the captured voices ring at once. Open the vials one after another, in time with the clock, and every voice finds its way home.
Die Wahrsagerin Orsolya hat die Ballgäst: The fortune teller Orsolya cursed the ball guests.
Die gestohlenen Stimmen werden in Phiole: The stolen voices are locked into vials of star glass.
Die neueste Karte: Der Stern berührt den: The newest chart: the star touches the crater rim on the night of the new moon. Beside it: “Align the mirrors. Twelve barrels of blood for the circle. He will come. He always comes.”
Die verschleierte Mieterin der Gießerei: The veiled tenant of the foundry is Miriam Vey with a borrowed face.
Dr. Pratt's Miracle Tonic is poison.
Drei Lampenanzünder verschwanden in zwöl: Three lamplighters vanished in twelve years, all in May, all near the canal. None was found. May is the month St. Ebba burned.
Du drehst den Spiegel, bis der Stern sic:
You turn the mirror until the star looks at itself. Then you call the names, one after another: Elias, Odile Varenne, the seven women, Lady Ashcombe, Molly, Benji. With every name a light breaks free and flies away over the rooftops, this time towards home.

The star grows pale. Starling stands up, the ledger pressed to his chest, and steps into the last ray of light. “Give Wexmoor my regards. And spare yourself the truth: I have already written it down, in four letters, and Price believes every word.” Then there is only light, and with it the only evidence vanishes.

At dawn Price and six constables stand outside the dome, an arrest warrant in hand. Marlowe steps between you. “He is my investigator until I say otherwise.” Quietly, just for you: “Three hours. That's all I can give.” She presses an envelope into your hand: a ticket and a letter of recommendation, signed with a stranger's name.
You pour the silver bath over the mirrors. The flakes come loose, rise like soot, and every scrap of darkness drifts out the door, down the street, into the villa quarter.

In the morning twelve people cast shadows again. Lucan Mews casts none. He sits in his cell and asks for a lamp so he can see whether he is still there at all.

Ada Whitlock gives you her old travel camera. “So you have something that only shows what is there.”
Du hast dem Revier geglaubt: Hester sei:
You believed the precinct: Hester ran away. Nobody keeps looking.

A week later Ivy finds her sister on the steps of the ruins. Hester breathes, but she never speaks again. She only hums.
Du hältst die Glocke ans Ohr. Durch das: You hold the bell to your ear. Through the humming you hear three notes from the North Gate, exactly the three it sings itself. The tower clock is playing Vey's song.
You strike until the bell cracks. It screams with seven voices as it does. When it's quiet, bronze lies everywhere, and beneath the shards there is no sound left.

Five of the seven women are found by the canal, mute. Two never are.

Miriam Vey is gone. On the floor where she lay is her borrowed face, empty as a shed skin.
Du schlägst zu. Der Spiegel springt, und:
You strike. The mirror cracks, and above the dome the star shatters with it. Shards of light rain down on the crater forest. Some lights find their way home, others go out as they fall.

When you turn around, Starling is gone and the ledger with him. On the desk lies a fifth letter, already addressed to the Kettlegate Courier: your cases, your evidence, your handwriting, deceptively real. Down the hill lanterns sway: Price, with a warrant for your arrest.

You flee through the crater forest. At the canal Kit waits on a coal barge and throws you a tarpaulin. “Heard you're famous now,” he says. At the goods station he slips you a ticket, and you'd rather not know where he got it.
Du schneidest die Fäden einzeln, und bei:
You cut the threads one by one, and with each you call a name. Up in the dormitory the children sit up, one after another, and cry because they don't know where they are.

The last thread doesn't lead upstairs but behind the loom. There Benji sleeps, curled up, his feet still black. When you call him, he opens his eyes and asks whether the man drank his water.

Price leads Miss Wren away. She smiles and says she saved the house. Edmund Thorne inherits and the first thing he does is withdraw the eviction.
Du zerschlägst die Spiegel, einen nach d:
You smash the mirrors one after another. With every crash a shadow drops to the floor and crawls away.

Most find their way back. Lady Ashcombe's doesn't. She lives, but she has avoided every light ever since.
Du öffnest die Phiolen eine nach der and:
You open the vials one after another, exactly as the clock strikes. Each voice rises as a small light and drifts away over the rooftops.

The next evening Madame Varenne sings again. Felix sits in a cell and hums, but it only sounds like a tired man now.

And high up in the tower, when everyone has gone, the bell strikes once by itself. In it a woman's voice, cold and calm: “Thank you, Felix. That will do.”
Durch den Kohlenschacht führen kleine, n: Small bare footprints lead through the coal chute. A child was in the counting house.
Durch den Kohlenschacht kam ein Kind in: A child came into the locked room through the coal chute. A child that someone sent.
Durch den alten Gaskanal gelangt man ung: Through the old gas tunnel you can get from the stage into the clock tower unseen. There the clock now sings Vey's melody.
Edmund Thorne hat seinen Onkel getötet,: Edmund Thorne killed his uncle to inherit.
Edmund wollte das Geld und hat seinen On: Edmund wanted the money and drowned his uncle.
A building plan of St. Ebba from the archive. A crypt is drawn beneath the chancel.
Ein Constable auf dem Weg nach St. Ebba: A constable on the way to St. Ebba
A constable carried Hester into the crypt. Rook was Vey's choirboy and not at his post on either night.
Ein Kind im Kontor: A child in the counting house
Ein Lied aus der Ruine hat Hester nachts: A song from the ruins lured Hester out at night.
Ein Notenblatt mit dem Augen-Siegel: „Sc: A sheet of music with the eye seal: “Sleep, child, the water watches”. Below, in ink: “for L., until you sing again”.
Ein Polizist hat Hester in die Krypta ge: A policeman carried Hester into the crypt.
Ein alter Gaskanal verbindet die Bühne d: An old gas tunnel connects the theatre's stage with the clock tower.
Ein neuer Stern steht über Kettlegate un: A new star stands over Kettlegate and comes closer every night.
Ein speckiges Heft voller Namen und Betr: A greasy notebook full of names and sums. No stamp of the market office, no signature. At the very bottom: “Silas, 2 shillings, as always.”
Ein um ein Haar falscher Ton bricht eine: A note just a hair off breaks a freshly cast bell.
Eine Frau mit Schleier hat die Gießerei: A veiled woman rented the foundry and paid with old choir silver.
Eine Frau namens Vey war hinter Elias' s: A woman named Vey was after Elias' silver lantern key.
Eine Frauenstimme dringt aus der Phiole,: A woman's voice escapes the vial, hoarse and far too close: “Felix, not so loud. You still sing like in St. Ebba.”
Eine Glocke für den Rostvater: A bell for the Rust Father
Eine leere Ginflasche, dick mit Staub be: An empty gin bottle, thick with dust. It has been lying here for days and has nothing to do with last night.
Elias Thorne verpfändete gestern einen s: Yesterday Elias Thorne pawned a silver lantern key. Bought the same evening by: “M. Vey”.
Elias pulled himself out of the canal.
Elias hat sich aus dem Wasser gezogen un: Elias pulled himself out of the water and walked to the pawnshop.
Elias ist nach dem Sturz zum Pfandhaus g: After the fall, Elias went to the pawnshop.
Elias rührt seit Jahren keinen Alkohol a: Elias hasn't touched alcohol in years.
Elias versteckt sich im Keller des Pfand: Elias is hiding in the pawnshop cellar.
Elias war betrunken und ist in den Kanal: Elias was drunk and fell into the canal.
Elias' Anzünderstange liegt am Südufer,: Elias' lighting pole lies on the south bank, the brass hook bent and wet up to the grip.
Entwürfe in Starlings winziger Schrift,:
Drafts in Starling's tiny handwriting, addressed to “F. D.”, “L. M.”, “I. W.” and “M. V.”. They all end the same:

“The harvest is ripe when the new investigator comes. Let him win.”
Es war eine ruhige Nacht. Niemand hat et: It was a quiet night. Nobody heard anything.
Ezra legt das Ohr an die Turmwand. „Seit: Ezra puts his ear to the tower wall. “For three nights something has been humming under the city, from the canal. Deep, like a bell not yet struck. It's waiting for something. For the new moon, if you ask me.”
Ezra zieht die Watte aus einem Ohr. „Die: Ezra pulls the cotton wool out of one ear. “The bell strikes wrong at night. Three notes instead of the hour. Always at 3:33. I've had the wool in since the clock started singing like that.”
Finn stiehlt nachts das Ochsenblut aus d: Finn steals the ox blood from the slaughterhouse at night.
Frische Kratzspuren an der Ufermauer unt: Fresh scratch marks on the embankment wall below the railing. Someone pulled himself out of the water here with bare hands.
Gekauft vor drei Wochen aus einem Nachla: Bought three weeks ago from an estate at the Canal Harbour. The seller is listed as: “M. V., for the choir”. The price was ridiculously low.
Greta: Das Zeichen des Chors: Greta: the sign of the choir
Greta: Der Junge im großen Mantel: Greta: the boy in the big coat
Greta: Die Frau im grauen Mantel: Greta: the woman in the grey coat
Hale hält das Glas gegen die Laterne. „E: Hale holds the glass against the lantern. “Duckweed. You only get that in the old Ashgrove canal, where the water stands still. In the harbour the salt eats it.”
Hester ist nicht weggelaufen. Veys Wiege: Hester didn't run away. Vey's lullaby for Lilian lured her into the ruins at night.
Hesters Medaillon liegt im Staub der Kap: Hester's locket lies in the dust of the chapel ruins. She was here that night, not on her way out of town.
Hinten im Einband klebt eine Liste des C: Glued inside the back cover is a list of the choir of St. Ebba, in Miriam Vey's handwriting. Among the boys, at the very bottom: “F. Dunmore, soprano. Stays, even after his voice breaks.”
Hinter Bess Hagans Stand steht ein Fass,: Behind Bess Hagan's stall stands a barrel that has been in the sun for days. The smell isn't coming from the harbour.
Hinter den Büchern, nur mit der Geistsic:
Behind the books, only visible with Spirit Sight, lies a ledger with stars instead of numbers.

“Harvest 1: light, Ashgrove Lane. Harvest 2: voices, North Gate. Harvest 3: bell sound, foundry. Harvest 4: shadows, Villa Ashcombe. Harvest 5: dreams, St. Brigid.”

Next to each entry is a date. They are the nights on which you closed your cases.
Holt hat Hester getragen und arbeitet fü: Holt carried Hester and works for Vey.
Hältst du die Platte gegen das Licht, be: Hold the plate against the light, and the thirteenth guest is made of patches that don't fit: Lady Ashcombe's hand, an officer's shoulder, a merchant's hat. Only the coat button is his own. Brass, like on Lucan's jacket.
Im Deckel der Spieldose eingraviert: „Ko: Engraved in the music box lid: “Come back to me, Lilian.”
Im Futter eines Mantels am Kostümständer: In the lining of a coat on the costume rack is a theatre ticket in the name of L. Crabb. The coat is covered in white porcelain dust, like in Pell's workshop.
Im Hinterhof hinter der Taverne, unter e: In the back yard behind the tavern, under a loose crate: a leather pouch with a dozen dice, all weighted. The letters S. M. are stitched into the leather.
Im Keller des Pfandhauses finden sie Eli:
In the pawnshop cellar they find Elias Thorne: shivering, but alive. Of Miriam Vey there is no trace.

Price mutters something that almost sounds like praise. Inspector Marlowe will want to hear from you.
Im Wäschekorb liegen Nachthemden, die Sä: In the laundry basket are nightgowns with wet, green hems. Duckweed, like in the canal behind the house.
Im singenden Splitter siehst du einen Ga: In the singing shard you see a passage full of gas pipes. A man with a script under his arm climbs a ladder, above him a clock face seen from inside.
Im verkohlten Glockenstuhl von St. Ebba: Nothing hangs in the charred belfry of St. Ebba any more. The mount was freshly sawn through, sawdust lies in the soot.
In Holts Schublade, obenauf, als hätte i: In Holt's drawer, right on top, as if someone had put it there: “For M. V. All ready. H.” The writing is stiff, as if written with the wrong hand.
In Lilians Zimmer sitzt ein Mädchen, dur: In Lilian's room sits a girl, translucent as breath on a windowpane. “Mama is building me a voice out of other voices,” she whispers. “I don't want a stranger's. I want to sleep.”
In Molls Jackentasche: neue Silbermünzen: In Moll's jacket pocket: new silver coins, wrapped in a piece of paper with the eye seal.
In Rooks Spind, unter einer zusammengele: In Rook's locker, under a folded choir robe: a delivery note. “40 wax candles, 2 cans of lamp oil. Delivery: Warehouse 7, Canal Harbour. Paid.”
In den Wannen der Dunkelkammer steht ein: In the darkroom trays is a silver bath that doesn't smell of silver but of cold glass. Dark flakes drift in it, turning away from your lamp.
In den letzten zwölf Jahren verschwanden: Over the last twelve years three lamplighters vanished, always in May.
In der Dose auf dem Regal liegen Mohnblü: In the tin on the shelf are poppy blossoms and something silvery, fine as cobwebs. Labelled in neat handwriting: “For quiet nights. I. W.”
In der Geistsicht kriecht kalter, türkis: In Spirit Sight, cold turquoise vapour creeps from the joints in front of the altar. There is a hollow beneath.
In der Geistsicht leuchten nackte, nasse: In Spirit Sight, bare wet footprints glow. They lead from the bridge to the pawnshop door.
In der Geistsicht siehst du es: In die R: In Spirit Sight you see it: an eye in a circle is scratched into the back of the mirror, the same sign as on Vey's seals. The glass fogs up as if it were breathing.
In der Gießerei wurde eine Glocke gegoss: A bell was cast at the foundry, and the voices of the seven singers are in the metal.
In der Glockengießerei Brannock wurde he: A new bell was secretly cast at the Brannock bell foundry.
In der Grube steht eine zerschlagene Gus: In the pit stands a smashed casting mould, as big as a man. Inside, the clay is smooth and scored with staff lines. A bell was cast here, and not long ago.
In der Kiste unter dem Stand liegen leer: In the crate under the stall are empty gin bottles, a jar of green ink, a roll of labels with medals and a brown bottle from the apothecary: laudanum.
In der Neumondnacht holt Starling den St: On the night of the new moon Starling brings the star down, at his observatory by the crater.
In der Neumondnacht will jemand den Ster: On the night of the new moon someone wants to bring the star down over the observatory.
In der Scherbe stehen hinter dir sieben: In the shard, seven women in choir robes stand behind you. They sing without sound. When you turn around, there is no one.
In die Gitterstäbe ist ein Auge in einem: An eye in a circle is scratched into the bars. Fresh. And from the outside, so by someone who comes and goes in the precinct.
In jedem deiner Fälle wurde etwas geernt: In each of your cases something was harvested: light, voices, bell sound, shadows, dreams. And everything leads to a man with lenses.
Ivy: Die Laterne am Grab: Ivy: the lantern at the grave
Jemand führt die Schlafwandler an Traumf: Someone leads the sleepwalkers on dream threads, and the end lies in the cellar of St. Brigid.
Jemand hat das Augen-Siegel von außen in: Someone scratched the eye seal into the precinct's cell bars from the outside.
Jemand schreibt anonyme Briefe, die dich: Someone is writing anonymous letters that make you the culprit of every case.
Jemand vereist die Laternen am Altmarkt: Someone is icing over the lanterns at the Old Market on purpose.
Jemand vereist mit Veys Zeichen die Late: Someone is icing the lanterns with Vey's sign, and choir equipment is turning up at the market. Not all the singers were in Warehouse 7.
Jonas Pell lets himself be led away without a word. Under his mask is only a scarred, friendly face.

A week later the next singer loses her voice. At 3:33 the tower clock sings, and at the precinct Marlowe no longer looks at you.
Josiah Thorne ist in seinem verschlossen: Josiah Thorne drowned in his locked, dry counting house.
Kupfermünzen, eine kleine Spur Richtung: Copper coins, a small trail heading east. Next to them a scrap of a far too large coat.
Sexton Anselm is robbing the graves.
Küster Anselm wird verhaftet. Er beteuer:
Sexton Anselm is arrested. He protests his innocence until his cash book is found. By then it is too late.

Hester is never found. In the ruins the singing goes on.
Lady Ashcombe hält eine Kerze neben sich: Lady Ashcombe holds a candle beside her. On the wall behind her there is nothing. “Since the ball. And I'm so tired. As if someone else were awake for me.”
Letzter Eintrag in Elias' Handschrift: „: Last entry in Elias' handwriting: “The woman in the grey coat was back. Wants the key. Says the lanterns belong to her.”
Lieferzettel im Salzfass: Delivery note in the salt barrel
Lilian Vey starb vor zwölf Jahren im Bra: Lilian Vey died twelve years ago in the fire of St. Ebba. At the grave her mother swore to bring her back, “whatever it costs”.
Lilian Veys Grab wurde geöffnet. Darin f: Lilian Vey's grave was opened. A small box is missing from it.
Lucan Mews war auf dem Ball, steht aber: Lucan Mews was at the ball, but is on no list and no plate.
Lucan setzt sich aus gestohlenen Schatte: Lucan is made of stolen shadows. Reverse the silver bath and they are given back.
Madame Orsolya is led away, laughing. “Tomorrow your shadow belongs to another,” she says to Price.

A week later Price has none either.
Madame Varenne ist nicht krank. Jemand h: Madame Varenne isn't ill. Someone has taken her voice.
Marktwart Grimes kassiert Schutzgeld von: Market warden Grimes collects protection money from the traders at the Old Market.
Marlowe lässt Miss Wren holen. Sie hört:
Marlowe has Miss Wren brought in. She listens to the accusations, folds her hands and says nothing.

What she did with the children, nobody can prove any more. But the children of St. Brigid sleep through the night again.
Marlowe lässt nach Miriam Vey fahnden, u:
Marlowe has a manhunt launched for Miriam Vey, and half the city searches for a woman with a borrowed face. Nobody looks up.

On the night of the new moon the star falls into the crater. In the morning the fourth anonymous letter lies on Price's desk, and this time everyone believes it. You are arrested right in the precinct.

On the way to prison the carriage stops at a building site. The door isn't locked. On the seat lie a ticket and a note in tiny handwriting: “Let him win. Later.”
Miriam Vey dreht ihr geliehenes Gesicht: Miriam Vey turns her borrowed face towards you. “I sang for a bell. He counted for a star. We were both wrong about who serves whom.”
Miriam Vey is wearing a borrowed face.
Miriam Vey will ihre tote Tochter Lilian: Miriam Vey wants to bring her dead daughter Lilian back.
Miss Pimm legt das Besucherbuch des Hosp: Miss Pimm produces the hospital visitor book, countersigned by the precinct: on both nights Holt sat at his sick wife's bedside until morning. Signed by the head nurse.
Miss Wren gibt den Kindern jeden Abend e: Every evening Miss Wren gives the children a tea with dream thread.
Miss Wrens Abendtee schickt die Kinder a: Miss Wren's evening tea sends the children wandering.
Mit dem ersten Glockenschlag will Vey ih: With the first stroke of the bell, Vey wants to call back her daughter Lilian.
Mit der Geistsicht siehst du sie: Von je: With Spirit Sight you see them: a thread rises from every pillow, thin as hair, and they all run together to the cellar door. One hangs loose. It leads to Benji's empty bed.
Moll hat Lilians Grab geöffnet, und Vey: Moll opened Lilian's grave, and Vey paid him for it. He fetched the music box for her.
Moll war vor dem Brand Bälgetreter der O: Before the fire, Moll worked the organ bellows in Miriam Vey's choir. He still owes her something.
Moll was paid with the choir's silver.
Molls Spaten: Das Blatt hat eine Kerbe w: Moll's spade: the blade has a notch like the marks at the grave, and yellow clay sticks to it.
Nur mit der Geistsicht zu erkennen: schw: Only visible with Spirit Sight: black sealing wax on the cobbles, stamped with an eye in a circle. It burns cold in your fingers.
Orsolya hat es vorhergesagt, also hat si: Orsolya predicted it, so she did it.
Owen schüttelt die Flasche gegen das Lic: Owen shakes the bottle against the light and sniffs it. “Gin, sugar, green ink and laudanum. Not poisonous. But whoever drinks it every day can't stop.”
Pratt verkauft gefärbten Gin mit Laudanu: Pratt sells coloured gin with laudanum. But Jack Hagan fell ill from the fish, not the tonic.
Price führt Edmund Thorne in Handschelle:
Price leads Edmund Thorne out of the counting house in handcuffs. He shouts that he was at the harbour. Nobody listens.

That same night a child in Ashgrove walks barefoot to the canal. Nobody sees it.
Price nimmt Jasper Reed fest, mit Flöte:
Price arrests Jasper Reed, flute and sack and all. Miss Wren thanks him with tears in her eyes.

The next night nobody plays outside the windows any more. And in the morning two children are missing.
Price notiert den Namen Vey. Drei Tage s:
Price notes down the name Vey. Three days later Elias is found in the pawnshop cellar. Frozen to death, in the middle of May.

Had you looked more closely, he might still be alive.
Price schreibt: „J. Thorne, Bankier, tot: Price writes: “J. Thorne, banker, dead in his counting house. Door bolted from inside. Lungs full of water, clothes dry. The nephew inherits everything. Suspect: nephew.”
Price schreibt: „Madame Orsolya, Wahrsag: Price writes: “Madame Orsolya, fortune teller, hired for the ball. Predicted death for guests. Three are now in bed. Case clear.”
Price schreibt: „Rostbrüder mit Zinnfäss: Price writes: “Rust Brothers seen with tin barrels at the Brannock foundry. Those lads cast chains, why not bells too. Suspicion: ritual of their Rust Father.”
Price stürmt Haus um Haus und findet Sch:
Price storms house after house and finds veils, silver, sheet music. No Vey.

On the night of the new moon a bell strikes beneath the city, once. All of Kettlegate wakes and doesn't know why it is weeping. In the morning the foundry is empty, and the chamber below has flooded.
Price stürmt die Sternwarte am hellen Mi:
Price storms the observatory in broad daylight. The dome is empty, the telescope dismantled, only a circle of dried blood on the floor.

On the night of the new moon the star sinks into the crater. All of Kettlegate sleeps badly, and in the morning nobody has their dream any more. Starling is never seen again.

In the afternoon Price finds everything the letters promised in your cabinet. Marlowe gets you out through the back door. “I can't protect you,” she says. “I can only buy you a ticket.”
Price und zwanzig Mann stürmen die Seile:
Price and twenty men storm the Ropers' Chapel at Anchor Yard. They find chains, rust water and angry men, but no bell.

That same night a bell strikes beneath the canal. Seven women are never found. The Rust Brothers don't forget who betrayed them.
Price verhaftet Felix noch im Souffleurk:
Price arrests Felix right there in the prompter's box. He smiles the whole time and says not a word.

When the constables later search the tower, they find only an empty shelf and glass dust. The voices stay lost. At 3:33 the clock keeps striking three notes.
Price verhaftet Lucan Mews im Atelier. E: Price arrests Lucan Mews at the studio. He smiles the whole time. The shadows stay lost, because nobody knows where he kept them. In the hall of mirrors at the North Gate, visitors go missing at night.
Price arrests Miss Wren at evening tea. She doesn't resist.

The children wander for three more nights, then the threads stop pulling. Benji stays missing. Nan searches for him at the canal every night.
Professor Starling wurde aus der Sternwa: Professor Starling was abducted from the observatory.
Quills Spiegel stammt aus dem Besitz von: Quill's mirror comes from the possessions of Vey's choir.
Rook hat sich für beide Nächte selbst zu: Rook put himself down for the watch in Ashgrove on both nights. Afterwards the entry was neatly struck out, without countersignature. Nobody replaced him.
Rook ist Veys Mann im Revier: Rook is Vey's man in the precinct
Rook war in den Nächten der Entführungen: Rook was not at his post on the nights of the abductions.
Rook wird abgeführt, der Chor ist zerstr:
Rook is led away, the choir is scattered. But when the constables search the warehouse, the belfry is empty. Vey took the bell with her.

Somewhere in Kettlegate she is waiting for the right night.
Rook wird in Ketten abgeführt. Die Glock:
Rook is led away in chains. The bell of St. Ebba lies in your hands, heavy and cold. Without it Vey's ritual is only a song without an end.

Miriam Vey has vanished into the canal. But for the first time you have taken something from her that she needs. Marlowe won't forget that.
Rooks Nächte führen zum Kanalhafen: Rook's nights lead to the Canal Harbour
Sergeant Holt secretly works for Vey.
Sergeant Holt gibt wortlos seine Dienstm:
Sergeant Holt hands in his badge without a word. The next morning Constable Rook doesn't show up for duty. His locker is empty.

That night a bell rings over Kettlegate that should no longer exist.
Sie schreibt mit zitternder Hand auf ihr: She writes on her pad with a trembling hand: “I hear myself singing. At night. Under the stage. It's my aria, but I'm not the one singing it.”
Sie schreibt: „Felix flüstert die Texte: She writes: “Felix whispers the lines so beautifully. Sometimes he hums along, very softly. An old church melody, three notes. I laughed at him.”
Sie schreibt: „Lionel Crabb. Ich habe ih: She writes: “Lionel Crabb. I had him thrown out because he drank. He swore he would come back, with a face nobody knows.”
Silas spielt im Ertrunkenen Mond mit gez: Silas plays with loaded dice at the Drowned Moon.
Silas zahlt Grimes jeden Freitag seinen: Silas pays Grimes his share every Friday. That's why nobody ever chased him out of Kettlegate.
Starling hat deine Fälle angestoßen. Was: Starling set your cases in motion. What you set free in the end flew to his star.
Starling hängt dir seine Ernte an. Du wa: Starling is pinning his harvest on you. You were at every crime scene, and every reward in your pocket is a piece of evidence.
Thorne ist nicht im Kontor ertrunken. Da: Thorne didn't drown in the counting house. The water came from Ashgrove, and it came to him.
Thorne wollte St. Brigid räumen. Miss Wr: Thorne wanted to evict St. Brigid. Miss Wren sent him a child in its sleep, with water from the canal.
Thorne wollte das Waisenhaus St. Brigid: Thorne wanted to have St. Brigid's orphanage evicted at the end of the month.
Tobias Lowe hat am Würfeltisch die Würfe: Tobias Lowe switched the dice at the dice table.
Totengräber Moll hat Lilian Veys Grab ge: Gravedigger Moll opened Lilian Vey's grave.
Um Mitternacht erklang vom Kanal ein Wie: At midnight a lullaby rang out from the canal.
Unter dem Altar der Ruine liegt eine Kry: There is a crypt beneath the altar of the ruins.
Unter dem Bühnenboden ist eine Falltür m: Under the stage floor is a trapdoor with fresh drag marks. Below, it smells of old gas, and very faintly you hear the ticking of a large clock.
Unter dem Kohlenschacht sind Abdrücke im: Under the coal chute are prints in the dust: small bare feet, barely longer than your hand. They go to the cellar door and back again. Without hurry.
Unter dem Kronleuchter werfen die Stühle: Under the chandelier the chairs cast shadows, the vases, the tables. Where guests stand on the plates there is no shadow, only a cold, bright patch.
Unter dem Textbuch im Souffleurkasten li: Under the script in the prompter's box lies an old sheet of music from St. Ebba. In the margin an eye in a circle and a list of singers' names. “O. Varenne” is neatly crossed out.
Unter dem Tisch, an dem Silas spielt, li: Under the table where Silas plays lies a lost die. One corner has been drilled and filled with lead. You throw it ten times. Eight sixes.
Unter der Haube der Laterne am südöstlic: Under the hood of the lantern at the south-east edge of the fountain an eye in a circle has been scratched, still fresh. The frost around the sign has grown in three rings. No night freezes like that.
Vey braucht die alte Glocke von St. Ebba: Vey needs the old bell of St. Ebba as the third piece of her ritual.
Vey hat die Glocke von St. Ebba in das L: Vey had the bell of St. Ebba brought to Warehouse 7. Without it she cannot complete the ritual.
Vey will Lilian keine Ruhe geben, sonder: Vey doesn't want to give Lilian rest, but a voice. Lilian herself doesn't want that.
Veys Chor besteht weiter. Sieben Sängeri: Vey's choir lives on. Seven singers have disappeared, but they are not dead.
Veys Chor stellt die schwarzen Kerzen vo: Vey's choir sets out the black candles in front of the Old Market chapel.
Von den Spiegeln im Kabinett ist das Sil: The silver has been scraped off the cabinet's mirrors in long strips, cleanly, with a fine blade. Whoever looks into the blind spots sees nothing. Not even themselves.
Von jedem Kind führt ein unsichtbarer Fa: An invisible thread leads from every child into the orphanage cellar.
Was deine Fälle befreit haben, ist nicht: What your cases set free did not go home, it rose up to the star.
Wenn Anselm Gräber plündert, hat er viel: If Anselm robs graves, maybe he also opened Lilian's grave.
Wenn die Rostbrüder die Glocke gießen, d: If the Rust Brothers are casting the bell, it's for a ritual of their own.
Wenn du bereit bist, nimm über die Stadt: When you're ready, take the train to Wexmoor via the city map. There is no going back afterwards. In Kettlegate Price has people searching for you: constables patrol the Old Market and the North Gate. Side tasks, bounties and danger zones stay open, but don't let yourself be seen.
Wer auf den Fotoplatten vom Ball zu sehe: Whoever appears on the photo plates from the ball has lost their shadow.
Wer die Platten im Silber der Kabinettsp: Whoever develops the plates in the silver of the cabinet mirrors traps the shadows of the people photographed.
Wer in der Neumondnacht in der Resonanzk: Whoever strikes a false note in the resonance chamber on the night of the new moon breaks the bell before it sings.
Zweimal haben Erwachsene ihre Taten auf: Twice, adults pinned their deeds on the apprentice, because nobody believes him anyway.
Zwischen Miriams Noten liegt eine Liste:: Among Miriam's music lies a list: seven women from the old choir, a note behind each name. All seven are crossed out. Below it: “Into the bell. Each in her place.”
Zwischen den Salzbrocken steckt ein Lief: Between the lumps of salt is a delivery note: “6 barrels of ox blood, Crow Bridge, pickup Wednesday. K.” Crow Bridge: that's where the Night Market is.
Zwischen den Zahnrädern steckt eine gesp: Between the cogwheels sits a cracked vial of dark glass with tiny lights drifting inside. Hold it to your ear and you hear a woman singing scales.
Zwölf Gäste, dazu „Miss A. Whitlock, Fot: Twelve guests, plus “Miss A. Whitlock, photography”. No assistant. Next to the list Lady Ashcombe has written: “The young man with the tripod was charming. Who was he?”
„Am Kanalhafen verkauf ich morgens. Da g: “I sell at the Canal Harbour in the mornings. Women in grey coats go into Warehouse 7 with candles in their baskets. And they don't come out before sunrise.”
„An der Spieldose und am Kreidekreis in: “Wool fibres were caught on the music box and on the chalk circle in the crypt. Dark blue, densely fulled. In Kettlegate only the constables get cloth like that.”
„An die Leitung von St. Brigid, Ashgrove: “To the management of St. Brigid, Ashgrove. The debt has not been settled. Eviction at the end of the month. J. Thorne.” Below, in a stranger's hand: “You will sleep where you put us.”
„Ausgerissen, ganz sicher. Die Kleine wo: “Ran off, for sure. The girl always wanted out of Kettlegate. I wouldn't waste time on it.”
„Barnaby J., festgenommen mit zwei Silbe: “Barnaby J., arrested with two silver candlesticks from the ruins of St. Ebba. Witness: none. Signed T. Rook.”
„Benji ist weg, seit einer Woche. In der: “Benji's been gone a week. The night before, he came back black as a chimney sweep and cried. He said he brought a man some water.”
„Constable Rook meint, das Mädchen sei e: “Constable Rook thinks the girl simply ran away. Happens at that age.”
„Das Auge? Damit haben die Damen vom Cho: “The eye? The ladies of the choir of St. Ebba sealed their letters with it. The choir mistress was called Miriam Vey.”
„Das Klopfen? Das war einer von euch. Ju: “The knocking? That was one of yours. Young face, blond hair under the helmet. Winked at me and scratched the eye into the bars.”
„Das Lied hat mich bei meinem Namen geru: “The song called me by my name, you understand? I just started walking. Into the water.”
„Das Silbergarn für den Tee? Ein Profess: “The silver yarn for the tea? A professor gave it to me. He said dreams nobody needs should go to the stars.”
„Das ist nicht mein Bad. Meins mische ic: “That isn't my bath. I mix mine myself, I know the smell. On the evening of the ball Lucan developed the plates, because I had to entertain the guests.”
„Den jungen Herrn mit dem Chemiekoffer?: “The young gentleman with the chemistry case? Drove him twice, at night, to the fair at the North Gate. He wanted me to wait. When he came back, my lantern cast no shadow of him.”
„Der Küster von St. Ebba? Würde mich nic: “The sexton of St. Ebba? Wouldn't surprise me if he robs graves. Odd fellow.”
„Der Maskenmacher Pell war am Abend in d: “The mask maker Pell was in the dressing room that evening. He doesn't speak, always wears a mask and handles plaster and lacquers. Probably poison in the powder. Arrest recommended.”
„Der alte Hauptstrang läuft vom Uhrturm: “The old main line runs from the clock tower under the square all the way to the theatre. It was bricked up thirty years ago. Bricked up! And last week the wall was open.”
„Der feine Pinkel mit dem lila Rock? Saß: “The toff in the purple coat? Sat in Anchor Yard all night losing. At four I saw him throw up into the canal. He wasn't anywhere else.”
„Der kleine Thomas. Miriam hat ihn bei s: “Little Thomas. Miriam took him in when his mother died. He would do anything for her. Anything.”
„Der Öllieferant vom Hafen hat bei mir S: “The oil supplier from the harbour exchanged silver with me. Stamped with the choir crest. He said it was payment for Warehouse 7.”
„Die Klappe vom Kohlenschacht stand offe: “The coal chute hatch was open. No grown-up fits through there, sir. I thought the coal man had been sloppy.”
„Die Silberleuchter? Stehen seit Wochen: “The silver candlesticks? They've been in my shop window for weeks. The sexton brought them to me. Why?”
„Die Splitter? Die hat mir der Professor: “The shards? The professor gave them to me. Voices keep best in star glass, he said. He only wanted to borrow them. Later.” Felix smiles. “He knew your name before you ever set foot in the theatre.”
„Die aus St. Brigid laufen nachts rum, M: “The St. Brigid lot walk about at night, mister. Eyes open, but they don't see nothin'. I took Molly by the hand and she didn't even flinch.”
„Drei Nächte haben die Öfen gebrannt, un: “For three nights the furnaces burned, and none of Brannock's men were there. Only women in white dresses who sang. I stuffed cotton in my ears and prayed.”
„Edmund Thorne, Neffe, Spielschulden bis: “Edmund Thorne, nephew, gambling debts up to his neck. Inherits counting house and fortune. Was supposedly ‘out’ that night.”
„Ein Bengel in einem viel zu großen Mant: “A rascal in a coat far too big for him. Kit's his name, always hangs about the east end.”
„Ein Herr mit Linsen hat mir gezeigt, wi: “A gentleman with lenses showed me how to lay shadows into silver. He only wanted to keep one of them. Every twelfth. That seemed fair to me.”
„Ein Junge mit Schlachterschürze wurde n: “A boy in a butcher's apron was seen at the theatre at night wearing a white mask. Probably the apprentice from the slaughterhouse. Petty thefts in the foyer.”
„Ein Mann hat mir die Maske geschenkt, d: “A man gave me the mask so I'd keep quiet. He had an actor's voice, really deep. I only put it on once, honest!”
„Ein Mensch ohne eigenen Schatten stirbt: “A person without a shadow of his own doesn't die, he just gets ... thin. Unless he takes some. Read it in a forbidden book. Please don't tell my professor.”
„Ein alter Mann, allein da draußen am Kr: “An old man, alone out there by the crater. Somebody took him. Probably for his lenses, they're worth a fortune.”
„Eine Dame mit Schleier. Hat die Gießere: “A lady with a veil. Rented the foundry for three nights and paid in silver, old coins stamped with an eye in a circle. She didn't want my men. She had her own singers.”
„Eine frische Glocke ist wie ein gespann: “A fresh bell is like a taut rope. Hold a note against it that's a hair off, and it snaps. I'll tune you a fork. But you have to get close enough.”
„Elias Thorne war ein Säufer, das weiß j: “Elias Thorne was a drunk, everyone knows that. Gin and canal, case closed.”
„Elias und Gin? Unsinn. Der hat seit sei: “Elias and gin? Nonsense. He hasn't touched a drop since his wedding.”
„Er hat mich getragen. Ich hab die Messi: “He carried me. I saw the brass buttons, like the constables have. And he hummed along. He knew the song.”
„Er ist unten im Keller. Halb erfroren,: “He's down in the cellar. Half frozen, keeps talking about a song. I didn't want her to find him.”
„Es ist dieser Rattenfänger. Er spielt n: “It's that rat catcher. He plays outside our windows at night. I've called the police three times already.”
„Felix Dunmore? Die schönste Knabenstimm: “Felix Dunmore? The most beautiful boy's voice St. Ebba ever had. Then his voice broke, and Miriam never looked at him again. He carried her sheet music for years. Just so she'd notice him.”
„Fragen Sie doch den Küster! Der verkauf: “Ask the sexton! He secretly sells things from the graves. I only dig.”
„Gestern Abend fragte eine Frau im graue: “Last night a woman in a grey coat asked about Elias. Whether he still has the old silver key. She called herself Vey.”
„Gestohlen? Ich habe die Leuchter selbst: “Stolen? I sold the candlesticks myself, to the pawnbroker in Ashgrove. For the roof beams. It's in the parish book.”
„Grimes geht jeden Freitag von Stand zu: “Every Friday Grimes goes from stall to stall. The coins jingle in his left pocket, not in the market cash box. That one sounds different, it has a lock.”
„Grün und Bauchkrämpfe? Das klingt nach: “Green and stomach cramps? That sounds like fish poisoning, not laudanum. Laudanum makes you sleepy, not green.”
„Hab 'nen Mann gesehen, klatschnass, der: “Saw a man, soakin' wet, crawlin' up the wall. Then he limped off towards the pawnshop.”
„Hab den Schornstein über der Gießerei g: “Swept the chimney above the foundry. Bell metal was hanging in it, copper and tin, still warm. And it rang when my broom touched it. Like an echo.”
„Heute Nacht? Nichts. Ich habe nichts ge: “Last night? Nothing. I heard nothing. Nothing at all.” He avoids your eyes.
„Heute früh war das Glas der Brückenlate: “Early this morning the glass of the bridge lantern was white as hoarfrost. In May! I saw it with my own eyes.”
„Holt. Ich hab ihn nachts im Keller gese: “Holt. I saw him in the cellar at night, with a letter. Don't tell anyone, he's my superior.”
„Ich hab auch Post bekommen. Drei Briefe: “I got mail too. Three letters. Interesting, where you were before we got there. Interesting, what you keep in your cabinet.”
„Ich hab aufgeschlossen, wie jeden Morge: “I unlocked, like every morning. He sat at the desk, the pen still in his hand. And there wasn't a drop on the carpet. Not a single one.”
„Ich hab drei Gäste untersucht. Puls sch: “I examined three guests. Weak pulse, no fever, no poison. And none of them casts a shadow, sir. I moved the lamp three times.”
„Ich hab für dich die Augen offen gehalt: “Kept me eyes open for ya. Moll was diggin' at night, back by the little graves. Then he went into the ruins with a box.”
„Ich habe allen in die Hand gesehen. All: “I looked into everyone's hand. Everyone but one. The boy with the box had no lines in his hand and no shadow under his feet. I said, tomorrow your shadow belongs to another. I meant: to him.”
„Ich spiele, damit sie zurückfinden! Rat: “I play so they find their way back! Rats follow the flute, sleeping children too. I lead them away from the canal, every night. I just never knew who sends them there.”
„Ich träume jede Nacht dasselbe. Ich geh: “I dream the same thing every night. I go to the water, and a woman hums. In the morning my feet are dirty. Miss Wren says that's from playing.”
„Ich war damals dabei, als junge Constab: “I was there back then, a young constable. Miriam Vey didn't cry. She sang. And said: every light I take brings you back a little.”
„Ihnen kann ich es sagen. Unter dem Alta: “I can tell you. There's a crypt under the altar. The entrance was bricked up after the fire. Or so I thought.”
„In der Brandnacht hat die Glocke von se: “On the night of the fire the bell rang by itself. Three times. Then came the flames. I never told anyone.”
„In der Nacht, als Hester verschwand, sa: “The night Hester disappeared, I saw the gravedigger with his lantern back by the children's graves.”
„Ja, ich erbe. Ja, ich hab Schulden. Und: “Yes, I inherit. Yes, I have debts. And yes, I hated him. But I was at the harbour drinking all night, ask anyone you like.”
„Jede Nacht ein Stück tiefer. Und er sum: “A bit lower every night. And it hums. Like my bells, only backwards.”
„Jede Nacht singt jemand in der Ruine. S: “Every night someone sings in the ruins. She calls me by my name. Today I'm going.”
„Jeden Abend Tee, das ganze Glas, sonst: “Tea every evening, the whole glass, or there's trouble. It tastes of honey and of nothing. Benji always tipped his into the flower pot. And then ... she noticed.”
„Jeden Morgen kurz vor sechs kniet eine: “Every morning shortly before six an old woman in black kneels in front of the chapel. Sets out candles and cries. I leave her be. Grief is nobody's business.”
„Jemand hat Lilians Grab geöffnet. Das K: “Someone opened Lilian's grave. The child lay in the earth with her music box. It's gone.”
„Jemand hat die Schlaghämmer neu gefeilt: “Someone refiled and moved the striking hammers. Clean work, a musician, not a clockmaker. The clock no longer plays the quarters, it plays a melody.”
„Jonas war die ganze Nacht bei mir oben: “Jonas was with me up in the tower all night. We recast the face of the tower figure. He never leaves until the bell strikes six, everyone knows that.”
„Keine Entzündung, kein Gift, nichts. Ih: “No inflammation, no poison, nothing. Her throat is cold as a dead woman's, but she lives. I've seen something like it once: with the singers from Warehouse 7.”
„Knox lädt nachts Fässer auf einen Karre: “Knox loads barrels onto a cart at night, I saw it. He said if I say anything, I'll be hanging on the hook next. Please don't tell the master.”
„Mein Jack hat Pratts Wundertonikum getr: “My Jack drank Pratt's Miracle Tonic, and he's been lying green in bed ever since! It's poison! I want that fellow hanged!”
„Miete, drei Nächte. Bezahlt in Silber d: “Rent, three nights. Paid in silver by M. V.” Below, in a different hand: “Rust Brothers' tin refused. The lady brings her own metal.”
„Miriam hat damals gesagt: Drei Stimmen: “Miriam said back then: three voices open the door. The light, the child, the bell. She has the lantern, she has the music box. Only the bell is missing.”
„Moll? Der zahlt seit einer Woche im Wir: “Moll? He's been paying in silver at the tavern for a week. A gravedigger! Where did he get it?”
„Moll? Hat mir beim Würfeln letzte Woche: “Moll? Paid me in silver at dice last week. Silver with a funny eye on it.”
„Nach dem Theater. Nach der Glocke. Nach: “After the theatre. After the bell. After the villa. Each time little lights rose up, all in the same direction. Out towards the crater.”
„Nachts lief ein Bulle Richtung Friedhof: “At night a copper walked towards the churchyard. No lantern. Blond. He was hummin', real quiet.”
„Nachts singt es in der Ruine. Ein Wiege: “At night there's singing in the ruins. A lullaby. And the other day a girl in a nightgown walked past me as if she hadn't seen me.”
„Nachts singt jemand an den Laternen. Ga: “At night someone sings at the lanterns. Very softly, always the same three notes. Afterwards it crackles like ice on a puddle. I told the police. They laughed.”
„Neben dem Kirchturm. Gestern war er noc: “Next to the church tower. Yesterday it wasn't there. At noon today you could see it in daylight.”
„Professor Starling ist seit drei Nächte: “Professor Starling has been missing for three nights. The observatory door was open. Price thinks he was abducted.”
„Resonanz, Ermittler! Jede Glocke hat ei: “Resonance, investigator! Every bell has a tone it can't bear. A shard of star glass in the casting or a false tuning fork at the rim, and the metal sings itself apart.”
„Rook kam vor einem halben Jahr aus der: “Rook came from the old chapel parish of St. Ebba half a year ago. Once told me he sang in the choir as a boy.”
„Rook sollte mich um Mitternacht ablösen: “Rook was supposed to relieve me at midnight. Twice. Twice he didn't come. I didn't report it, you don't rat on a colleague.”
„Schwarze Kerzen im Halbkreis, jeden Mor: “Black candles in a semicircle, every morning. After St. Ebba everyone knows who does such things. It's Vey's choir. They are mocking the house of God.”
„Sie hat bezahlt. Ich sollte die Spieldo: “She paid. I was to fetch the little one's music box. It's down there. Under the altar. The girl too.”
„Sie hat die Glocke nicht oben aufgehäng: “She didn't hang the bell up top. Down below, in the old resonance chamber where my grandfather tested the tones. At the new moon, she said. The first strike belongs under the earth.”
„Sie hat jedem von uns in die Hand geseh: “She looked into each of our hands and said: tomorrow your shadow belongs to another. We laughed. Who's laughing now?”
„Sie knien am Kanal und halten die Hände: “They kneel at the canal and hold their hands in the water. All the same. As if they were scooping something, for someone else.”
„Sie waren bei jedem Fall als Erster am: “You were first at the scene in every case. You knew things only the culprit could know. In your pockets are a dream spool, a voice vial, a shard from the crater.” Marlowe puts the letter down. “He knows your evidence better than I do. And the paper has a watermark. A star.”
„Sieben Kerzen für sieben Jahre mit Walt: “Seven candles for seven years with Walter. He played the organ in the Old Market chapel before Miriam took him to St. Ebba. Black, because white candles are for the living.”
„Sieben Stimmen, eine für jedes Jahr, da: “Seven voices, one for every year she should have lived. When the bell strikes, Lilian will answer. She must. I have built her a voice.”
„Sieben meiner Kundinnen sind weg. Alle: “Seven of my customers are gone. They all used to sing in St. Ebba, I know because I washed their white robes. Last week each of them collected her robe. And none ever came back for her washing.”
„Silas, der Spieler. Seine Würfel klinge: “Silas, the gambler. His dice sound wrong. Two click bright like bones, the others dull. Lead. He swaps them when he coughs.”
„So'n Singsang, ganz leise, vom Wasser h: “Some singin', real quiet, from the water. Middle of the night. Gave me proper chills.”
„Sternglas hält Licht fest. Und Licht is: “Star glass holds on to light. And light is only a kind of vibration, isn't it? Whoever grinds it finely enough can lock a sound inside as well. A voice, for instance. In theory.”
„Thomas Rook? Er sang die Soli. Miriam l: “Thomas Rook? He sang the solos. Miriam loved him like a son. After the fire he stood in front of the ruins for days and wept.”
„Tobias hat Schulden, seit sein Bruder t: “Tobias has had debts since his brother died. And yesterday he threw a jug at Silas. Whoever always loses starts cheating at some point.”
„Um Mitternacht flackerten alle Laternen: “At midnight all the lanterns flickered, and a humming came from the canal. An old lullaby.”
„Und da war Flöte. Jedes Mal. Der Ratten: “And there was a flute. Every time. The rat catcher, the one with the sack.”
„Vor einer Woche stand eine Fremde in me: “A week ago a stranger stood at my door. Younger than Miriam, prettier. But she hummed Lilian's lullaby, wrong in exactly the way only my sister hums it. She bought herself a face. From the grey sisters, they say.”
„Wenn ich spiele, spür ich einen Zug, wi: “When I play, I feel a pull, like on a fishing line. From every child downwards. Into the cellar of St. Brigid. I never dared to go down there.”
„Wer Grimes nicht zahlt, dessen Stand fä: “Whoever doesn't pay Grimes finds their stall knocked over at night. Mine has fallen over twice already. And the morning after, he stood there laughing.”
„Wir haben vor seinem Kontor gestanden,: “We stood outside his counting house with signs. He wanted to evict the orphanage. The day before his death the head of the home came out, very calm. She said: he'll think it over. In his sleep.”
„Wir sind der Schleierfrau nachgegangen,: “We followed the veiled woman 'cause she pays in silver. By the canal the wind lifted her veil. Her face slipped, mister. Like wet paper. There was another one underneath.”
